vaccines.title: BCG Vaccine
why_important: Protects against severe forms of tuberculosis.
what_to_expect: Small injection on the upper arm.
tips: Give as soon as possible after birth.

vaccines.title: Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV-1)
why_important: First dose of routine polio protection.
tips: Give together with Pentavalent-1, PCV-1, and Rotavirus-1.

vaccines.title: Pentavalent Vaccine (DPT-HepB-Hib-1)
why_important: Protects against diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, hepatitis B, and Hib.
what_to_expect: May cause mild fever or soreness.
tips: Give alongside OPV-1, PCV-1, and Rotavirus-1.

vaccines.title: Pneumococcal Vaccine (PCV-1)
why_important: Protects against pneumonia, meningitis, and ear infections.
tips: Can be given together with Pentavalent-1 and OPV-1.

vaccines.title: Rotavirus Vaccine (Rota-1)
why_important: First dose against severe diarrhoea from rotavirus.
tips: Do not give if child is >15 weeks at first dose.

vaccines.title: Pentavalent Vaccine (DPT-HepB-Hib-2)
tips: Can be given with OPV-2, PCV-2, Rotavirus-2.

vaccines.title: Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV-3)
tips: Give with Pentavalent-3, PCV-3, IPV, and Rotavirus-3.

vaccines.title: Pentavalent Vaccine (DPT-HepB-Hib-3)
why_important: Final primary dose for these diseases.

vaccines.title: Rotavirus Vaccine (Rota-3)
why_important: Completes protection against severe rotavirus diarrhoea.
tips: Must be given before 32 weeks of age.

vaccines.title: Measles–Rubella Vaccine (MR-1)
tips: Given with Yellow Fever at the same visit.

vaccines.title: Yellow Fever Vaccine
why_important: Protects against yellow fever, now part of routine schedule in Uganda.
tips: Single lifetime dose; given with MR-1.

vaccines.title: Measles–Rubella Vaccine (MR-2)
why_important: Provides long-term measles and rubella protection.
